correctness.rationale: For a unilateral weighted shift with squared weights a_n, W*W and WW* are shifted diagonal operators, so the self-commutator has diagonal (a_0,a_1-a_0,...). Monotone a_n decreasing to zero gives trace norm 2a_0. The chosen weights tend to zero, hence compactness, and their product formula gives spectral radius zero. Their singular values are the weights, while every finite power of 1/log(n+2) has divergent sum, so W lies in no finite Schatten class.

originality.rationale: Kittaneh's 1991 paper explicitly leaves open whether the finite-p nilpotent Schatten implication survives under quasinilpotence. The consulted later self-commutator and weighted-shift literature did not locate an explicit resolution of that question. The standard weighted-shift formulas themselves are not claimed as new; residual risk from older unadvertised observations is documented.

value.rationale: One elementary compact quasinilpotent example simultaneously separates trace-class self-commutator from every finite Schatten class, sharply showing that Kittaneh's nilpotence hypothesis cannot be weakened to quasinilpotence at any finite ideal scale. The monotone-weight mechanism is reusable and allows arbitrarily slow singular-value decay.
